questions.prompt: What is a double opt-in introduction?
questions.answer: Both parties separately agree before the private connection is made.
questions.feedback: It is a practical consent approach, not a universal legal rule.

questions.prompt: Does agreeing to an introduction authorise all contact details?
questions.answer: No; share only appropriate authorised information.

questions.feedback: Wait or use a legitimate alternative.

questions.prompt: What does an introduction not guarantee?
questions.answer: A meeting, endorsement, referral or future relationship.

scoring.knowledge: 1 point per correct answer; formative only.
scoring.practice: Designs permission-based introductions with clear purpose, minimum information, realistic expectations and refusal handling.
scoring.transfer: Create a fictional introduction workflow with separate permission requests, a minimum-information record, an introductory message and two refusal cases. Identify when organisational privacy advice is needed and why an introduction is not a guaranteed meeting.
scoring.pass: All mapped criteria require Level 2 evidence; no averaging away omissions or safety-critical criteria. No automatic competency award.
